segments.text: A one-sample t-test is a hypothesis test that checks whether a sample mean is significantly different from a claimed population mean, when the population standard deviation is unknown.
segments.caption: A one-sample t-test is a hypothesis test that checks whether a sample mean is significantly different from a claimed population mean, when the population standard deviation is unknown.

segments.text: Use it for one average versus a claim, when sigma is unknown, especially with small samples.

scenes.title: Steps 1 and 2: one tail or two

segments.text: Step one: H zero says the average is two hundred milliliters.
segments.caption: Step one: H0 says the average is 200 ml.

segments.text: H one is two-tailed if it could differ either way, or one-tailed if we only ask: is it less?
segments.caption: H1 is two-tailed if it could differ either way, or one-tailed if we only ask: is it less?

segments.text: Step two: alpha, five percent. Two-tailed splits it, two point five percent per tail. One-tailed puts all five percent on the left. We'll do both.
segments.caption: Step two: alpha, 5%. Two-tailed splits it, 2.5% per tail. One-tailed puts all 5% on the left. We'll do both.

segments.text: Step three: the formula. t equals x-bar minus mu, over s over root n.
segments.caption: Step three: the formula. t equals x-bar minus mu, over s over root n.

segments.text: It's the z formula, with one change: s, the sample standard deviation, replaces sigma.
segments.caption: It's the z formula, with one change: s, the sample standard deviation, replaces sigma.

segments.text: First, s. Square each bottle's distance from one ninety-eight: twenty-five, nine, one, one, zero, one, one, nine, twenty-five. They add up to seventy-two.
segments.caption: First, s. Square each bottle's distance from 198: 25, 9, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 9, 25. They add up to 72.

segments.text: Divide by n minus one, which is eight: that's nine. The square root of nine is three. So s is three.
segments.caption: Divide by n - 1, which is 8: that's 9. The square root of 9 is 3. So s is 3.

segments.text: Standard error: s over root n, three over root nine, which is three over three: one.
segments.caption: Standard error: s over root n, 3 over root 9, which is 3 over 3: 1.

segments.text: So t equals one ninety-eight minus two hundred, over one: t equals minus two. The same number we got with z!
segments.caption: So t equals 198 minus 200, over 1: t equals -2. The same number we got with z!

segments.text: Degrees of freedom: n minus one, which is eight.
segments.caption: Degrees of freedom: n - 1, which is 8.

segments.text: With so few bottles, the t curve has fatter tails than the normal curve, so the cut-offs are bigger.
segments.caption: With so few bottles, the t curve has fatter tails than the normal curve, so the cut-offs are bigger.

segments.text: Two-tailed first. In the t table, row eight, column two-tailed zero point zero five: the critical value is two point three zero six.
segments.caption: Two-tailed first. In the t table, row 8, column two-tailed 0.05: the critical value is 2.306.

segments.text: So the critical region is beyond plus or minus two point three zero six.
segments.caption: So the critical region is beyond ±2.306.

segments.text: Two is below two point three zero six, so p is above zero point zero five. Software says zero point zero eight.
segments.caption: 2 is below 2.306, so p is above 0.05. Software says 0.08.

segments.text: Our t of minus two is not in the critical region. Two-tailed, we fail to reject H zero.
segments.caption: Our t of -2 is not in the critical region. Two-tailed, we fail to reject H0.

segments.text: With z, minus two was enough. With t, it isn't: fatter tails need stronger evidence.
segments.caption: With z, -2 was enough. With t, it isn't: fatter tails need stronger evidence.

segments.text: Now one-tailed: is the average less than two hundred?
segments.caption: Now one-tailed: is the average less than 200?
